original_question: An O* group is one in which every partial order extends to a total order making the group a totally ordered group. Can every orderable group be embedded in an O* group?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.15: whether every orderable group can be embedded in an O∗-group. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target very closely: it uses the correct class O∗-groups, gives essentially the right extension property, and asks the same universal embedding question over all orderable groups as Problem 3.15. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
missing_details: In the paper, an O∗-group is introduced in Section 3, and “ordered/orderable” is the two-sided notion, since these groups are treated as special cases of both ℓ-groups with total order and right-ordered groups whose order is also preserved by multiplication on the left. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

The intended “partial order” is a partial order in the ordered-group sense, not an arbitrary set-theoretic partial order on the underlying set; this is implicit from the surrounding ordered-group context and the parallel notation for right partial orders earlier in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

The paper asks only for a group embedding into some O∗-group; it does not ask for a chosen order on the original group or for an order-preserving embedding. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the quantifiers should be explicit: for every orderable group G, does there exist an O∗-group H and an injective homomorphism G -> H? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

It is worth distinguishing this from the neighboring Problem 3.19, which is different: there the ambient group is only required to be orderable, and the extension property is stated for G-invariant partial orders on the embedded subgroup H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
refined_question: Does every orderable group G—that is, every group admitting a two-sided total order—admit an injective group homomorphism G -> H into some O∗-group H, where an O∗-group is a group such that every partial order on H compatible with the group structure extends to a total order making H a totally ordered group (an o-group)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
justification: This is exactly Problem 3.15 in Section 3, after the paper introduces O∗-groups. It is closer to 3.15 than to the neighboring Problem 3.19: your draft asks whether the ambient group itself can be taken to be an O∗-group, whereas 3.19 asks for an embedding into an orderable group with an extension property only for G-invariant partial orders on the embedded subgroup. The nearby comment for 3.15 records partial progress—free groups are embeddable in O∗-groups—which confirms that 3.15 is the right narrow target. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
